EMPIRICAL RESEARCH PLAN  

------------------------------------------------------------  
1. Identification Strategy  
Strategy: Difference-in-Differences (panel event-study version).  
Rationale:  

• The Lehman failure was a sharp, externally-imposed shock to the wholesale funding market, plausibly exogenous to any individual bank’s lending plans.  
• Banks differed ex-ante in their exposure to that market (wholesale-funding share).  
• We observe the same banks before and after the shock at quarterly frequency, allowing us to difference out time-invariant bank characteristics with bank fixed effects and common macro shocks with time fixed effects.  
• An event-study specification (interacting bank exposure with a full set of quarter dummies) will allow us to (i) test the key parallel-trends assumption and (ii) trace dynamic effects.  

------------------------------------------------------------  
2. Treatment and Control  

Treatment variable  
  “High wholesale funding” bank = 1{ Wholesale Funding Ratioᵢ,(Q2 2008) ≥ sample median }.  
  (ratio = short-term market borrowings ÷ total liabilities; measured the last full quarter before Lehman.)  

Control group  
  “Low wholesale funding” banks: Wholesale Funding Ratio below median.  
  Robustness: use terciles, continuous interaction, or leave ratio continuous.  

Treatment timing / event date  
  Event date: Lehman bankruptcy (15 Sep 2008).  
  Operational post period: 2008:Q4 onward (first full post-Lehman quarter).  
  Pre period: 2006:Q1–2008:Q2 (exclude 2008:Q3 as a fuzzy transition in robustness checks).  
  We will estimate β in:  

     log(New Loans)ᵢt = αᵢ + γ_t + β (Highᵢ × Post_t) + Xᵢt′δ + εᵢt  

where αᵢ = bank FE, γ_t = quarter FE.

------------------------------------------------------------  
3. Key Identifying Assumptions  

A1  Parallel trends: In the absence of the shock, lending by high- and low-wholesale banks would have evolved similarly.  
     Plausibility: Prior to 2008:Q3 the two groups faced the same macro environment; visual inspection of pre-event trends and formal pre-trend tests in the event study help validate.  

A2  No simultaneous, group-specific shocks: No other intervention hit only highly wholesale-funded banks at the same time.  
     Plausibility: Major contemporaneous policies (TARP CPP capital injections, FDIC TLGP guarantees) were broadly available, not targeted only to one group. We will control for capital injections at the bank-quarter level.  

A3  Stable unit treatment value (SUTVA): Lending by low-wholesale banks is not directly affected by the stress experienced by high-wholesale banks except through equilibrium price effects common to all (so captured by γ_t).  
     Plausibility: Some spill-overs are possible but will bias toward zero (low banks may expand lending), so estimates of β will be conservative.  

------------------------------------------------------------  
4. Major Threats and Mitigations  

T1  Differential loan demand shocks (regional/industry).  
     Fix: Use loan-level DealScan data and include borrower-industry×quarter fixed effects, or aggregate bank-level analysis controlling for geographic loan mix shares interacted with time.  

T2  Pre-existing trends (violation of A1).  
     Fix: Plot and test coefficients for −8…−1 quarters in event study; drop banks with fast pre-crisis growth; re-weight via inverse-probability-weighted DID.  

T3  Government support (TARP capital, Fed liquidity) correlated with funding structure.  
     Fix: Control directly for amount of TARP capital received and Fed discount-window/TAF usage; estimate results after subtracting TARP quarters; or instrument funding shock with 2006 county-level retail-deposit growth interacted with crisis dummy (robustness IV).  

------------------------------------------------------------  
5. R Code Outline  

```r
# ---- 0. Packages ----
library(data.table)
library(fixest)
library(ggplot2)

# ---- 1. Load and merge data ----
# Assume two csv files: fr_y9c.csv (bank balance sheet) and dealscan.csv (loan level)
y9  <- fread("fr_y9c.csv")      # bank_id, date (yyyyq), assets, core_dep, st_borrow, loans_out
ds  <- fread("dealscan.csv")    # loan_id, bank_id, date, amount

# Aggregate DealScan to bank-quarter new syndicated loan volume
ds_q <- ds[, .(new_loans = sum(amount)), by = .(bank_id, date)]

# Merge
dt  <- merge(y9, ds_q, by = c("bank_id","date"), all.x = TRUE)
dt[is.na(new_loans), new_loans := 0]

# ---- 2. Construct variables ----
dt[, wholesale_ratio := st_borrow / (st_borrow + core_dep)]     # liabilities proxy
# Tag pre-period wholesale ratio (Q2 2008)
pre_ratio <- dt[date == "2008Q2", .(pre_wr = wholesale_ratio), by = bank_id]
dt <- merge(dt, pre_ratio, by="bank_id")

median_wr <- median(pre_ratio$pre_wr, na.rm = TRUE)
dt[, high_wholesale := as.integer(pre_wr >= median_wr)]

dt[, post := as.integer(date >= "2008Q4")]

dt[, ln_new_loans := log1p(new_loans)]   # log(1+loans) to keep zeros

# Controls
dt[, capital_ratio := tier1_capital / assets]   # assuming var exists
dt[, size_ln := log(assets)]

# ---- 3. Main DID regression ----
did_main <- feols(ln_new_loans ~ post * high_wholesale + capital_ratio + size_ln |
                    bank_id + date,
                  cluster = ~bank_id, data = dt)
summary(did_main)

# ---- 4. Event-study ----
# Create relative-time dummies: -8 to +6 quarters around Lehman
lehman_q <- "2008Q3"
dt[, rel_q := as.integer(factor(date, 
                     levels = sort(unique(date))) - 
                     which(sort(unique(date)) == lehman_q))]

# keep window
dt_es <- dt[rel_q >= -8 & rel_q <= 6]

# interact dummies with high_wholesale (omit -1)
for(k in c(-8:-2,0:6)){
  dt_es[, paste0("D",k) := as.integer(rel_q == k) * high_wholesale]
}

fml <- as.formula(
  paste("ln_new_loans ~", 
        paste(paste0("D", c(-8:-2,0:6)), collapse = " + "),
        "+ capital_ratio + size_ln | bank_id + date"))
es <- feols(fml, cluster=~bank_id, data=dt_es)
iplot(es, ref.line = 0)   # plot of dynamic effects

# ---- 5. Robustness: continuous treatment ----
did_cont <- feols(ln_new_loans ~ post:pre_wr + capital_ratio + size_ln |
                    bank_id + date,
                  cluster = ~bank_id, data = dt)
summary(did_cont)
```

------------------------------------------------------------  
6. Expected Results  

Prior: Banks with high wholesale funding cut lending sharply. Expect β < 0.  
Magnitude guess: a one-offswitch from low→high wholesale (binary version) lowers new syndicated lending by 20–30 percent during 2008:Q4–2009:Q2. In continuous spec, a 10 ppt higher wholesale ratio reduces lending by roughly 5 percent.  

------------------------------------------------------------  
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (Difference-in-Differences)  

C1  Pre-treatment parallel trends visually and statistically verified ….. 0.8  
C2  No simultaneous group-specific shocks (exogeneity of treatment) …… 0.6  
C3  No differential compositional changes (bank exits/mergers) ………… 0.7  
C4  No spill-overs between groups (SUTVA) ………………………………… 0.6  
C5  Robust standard errors and multiple robustness checks ……………… 1.0  

Overall self-score ≈ 3.7/5 → reasonably credible but still demands careful robustness work.
